1. The Henry's law constant for the solubility of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ gas in water at 298 K is $1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~atm}$. The mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ in air is 0.8 . The number of moles of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ from air dissolved in 10 moles of water at 298 K and 5 atm pressure is
(A) $4.0 \times 10^{-4}$
(B) $4.0 \times 10^{-5}$
(C) $5.0 \times 10^{-4}$
(D) $4.0 \times 10^{-6}$

Sol. (A)
$\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}} \chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}$
$0.8 \times 5=1 \times 10^{5} \times \chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}$
$\chi_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=4 \times 10^{-5} \quad$ (in 10 moles of water)
$\Rightarrow 4 \times 10^{-5}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}+10}$
$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} \times 5 \times 10^{-5}+4 \times 10^{-4}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}}=4 \times 10^{-4}$

7. Among the electrolytes $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}, \mathrm{CaCl}_{2}, \mathrm{Al}_{2}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)_{3}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$, the most effective coagulating agent for $\mathrm{Sb}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{3}$ sol is
(A) $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}$
(B) $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$
(C) $\mathrm{Al}_{2}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)_{3}$
(D) $\mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{Cl}$

Sol. (C)
As $\mathrm{Sb}_{2} \mathrm{~S}_{3}$ is a negative sol, so, $\mathrm{Al}_{2}\left(\mathrm{SO}_{4}\right)_{3}$ will be the most effective coagulant due to higher charge density on $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ in accordance with Hardy-Schulze rule.
Order of effectiveness of cations: $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}>\mathrm{Ca}^{++}>\mathrm{Na}^{+}>\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}$
